newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists back European growth pact.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists back European growth pact.

text.p: The Socialist Party will seek a "growth pact" with its European partners rather than strict adherence to economic criteria if it wins France's May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, party spokesman Francois Hollande said on Wednesday.

"It is clear that we will not meet the three percent, no more than the Germans, the Italians or the others," Hollande told Reuters in an interview, referring to the Maastricht Treaty's required three percent ratio of public deficits to Gross Domestic Product to qualify for European monetary union.
"Between three percent and 3.5 percent, we cannot imagine putting off a single currency, or even stop moving towards it, just because of a few tenths of a percent," he said.

"What we would like -- and this could be the most difficult element of negotiations with our partners -- would be a growth pact, an agreement to get economic activity started again," he said in the interview.

Opinion polls show the opposition Socialists now lagging behind the current centre-right majority in the two-round election, but within striking distance of winning power if they make some gains in the coming weeks and team up with other parties on the Left.

Hollande said the austerity measures that would be needed to stick to a strict interpretation of the monetary union requirements might have the inadvertent effect of "further weakening the ties that bind together the people of Europe."
Monetary union "must be a factor for growth," he said.
Hollande also said in the interview that the Socialists favoured raising the minimum wage and did not rule out negotiations with civil servants aimed at wage increases if they won the election.
"An increase in purchasing power can be achieved in many ways," including a reduction in value added tax (VAT), creation of more jobs and raising salaries, he said.
"The more people you bring into the system, the more people have salaries and the more you boost consumer spending."
The Socialists would like to lower the VAT to 5.5 percent from its current 20.6 percent for some basic necessities such as housing-related expenses like home repair and rehabilitation, he said.
But he said the party had not yet calculated the cost of such a measure.
